critical_evidence.evidence: No borescope mentioned. The 3.2 M96 at 90k is susceptible to bore scoring, and low recent use (~1,700 mi in two years) means oil consumption history tells little.
No IMS retrofit and no engine number mentioned. A 2005 987.1 likely carries the smaller single-row bearing with the highest failure rate; the engine number is needed to confirm.
Oil changes are listed (11/2024, 07/2026), but there is no filter cut or photo.
An 'Inspection / Service @90k 07/2025' is claimed, but there is no scan printout, cam deviation values or over-rev counts.

The hardtop is fitted in every attached photo, so the soft top is never shown. No top-cycle video and no drain or footwell carpet-edge photos. Visible footwell carpet looks dry, but edges were not examined.
Only a coolant flush (@91k, 08/2026) is claimed, without receipt. There is no record of water pump, thermostat, expansion tank or front radiator/condenser work.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is present: VIN published and decoded consistently, plus a dated maintenance list with mileages. The evidence half is missing: no receipts, no Carfax copy despite a disclosed damage entry, no engine number or IMS paperwork, and no records before 89k miles.

condition.rationale: Photos show straight, glossy paint and a tidy frunk. The interior has moderate bolster creasing and scuffs, and the seller discloses minor chips. Nothing mechanical is proven either way: no borescope, scan, underside, tire dates or soft-top evidence. The claimed AOS and engine mounts are unreceipted.

price_value.rationale: The $23,000 ask is far above the $13,232-$16,403 fair-value estimate. The comps are thin (two 2006 sales) but include a similar-mileage 2006 S at $13,100. The unaddressed IMS question on a 2005 engine, the unexplained Carfax damage and missing receipts pull value down further.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual with a genuine point of view, and the ask is under the $27,000 ceiling but above the $10,000-$19,000 ideal band. As a bridge it is weak: a 2005 M96 carries the highest IMS/bore risk, and resale in 6-24 months from this entry price is poor. The buyer context also treats 987 manuals as keepers, not bridge cars.

logistics.rationale: Tucson is a fly-out and a long one-day drive home. A private seller in a city with Porsche specialists makes a PPI plausible, but access is not stated. CA smog/registration from Arizona is likely feasible but unconfirmed.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits: 6-speed manual, S, Sport Chrono Plus (clock visible), OEM hardtop, and a claimed rare Dark Olive over Sand Beige. These are offset by taste-specific, cheap-to-moderate modifications (gold aftermarket wheels, gold-painted vents, aftermarket head unit with loose wiring) that narrow the resale audience.

ppi_focus: Borescope all six cylinder walls for scoring; oil filter cut for metallic debris
Durametric/PIWIS: fault memory, cam deviation per bank, over-rev counts in ranges 1-6 (short shifter plus manual)
IMS/RMS area at the bellhousing: seep vs active drip; confirm engine number for bearing type
Cooling system: water pump weep, expansion tank and cap crust, coolant pipes, front radiators/condensers and debris packing

Remove the hardtop and cycle the soft top; check cables, rams for hydraulic leaks, top/cowl drains, and carpet and module areas for water staining
Clutch engagement point and DMF judder; short shift kit installation and linkage bushings
Suspension: front control arms and coffin-arm bushings, top mounts, tie rods; alignment and ride height
Aftermarket CarPlay wiring (loose footwell cable) and a battery drain check
Tire date codes, sizes and matching; wheel fitment and offsets

evidence.mission_note: It meets the manual and point-of-view requirements, but a 2005 M96 with no IMS or borescope evidence is not a low-risk bridge, and buying well above fair value undermines resale in 6-24 months. The buyer's own framing places 987 manuals in the keeper category rather than the bridge category.
evidence.rationale: The VIN is published and decodes as a 2005 Boxster S 3.2 consistent with the listing, and photos confirm a genuine manual, the Sport Chrono Plus clock and the OEM hardtop. The maintenance history is a dated list from 11/2024 onward (AOS, engine mounts, coolant, brake fluid, oil) with no receipts attached and nothing before 89k miles. Observed issues are a seller-disclosed Carfax damage entry with no report or repair documentation, disclosed paint chips, and taste-specific aftermarket wheels, painted vents and a CarPlay unit with loose wiring visible in the footwell. None of the six model-critical items is evidenced. Most important for a 2005 engine: there is no engine number or IMS retrofit record and no borescope, and water pump and soft-top history are silent. The $23,000 ask is well above the $13,232-$16,403 fair-value estimate, though the comp set is only two 2006 sales. Condition beyond the glossy exterior photos remains open until a Porsche-specialist inspection.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the engine number, the Carfax report and invoices for the listed work, and ask to book a PPI at a Tucson Porsche specialist that includes a borescope, oil filter cut and Durametric over-rev and cam deviation readout.
